tldr: Foundry Managed Compute is now generally available for serving open models on dedicated GPUs, making managed hosting a new option to compare with operating your own GPU fleet.
The Azure Functions OpenAI Extension reaches end of support on April 20, 2027; plan a migration to the appropriate direct SDK.
A test using two million trackable canaries found that sensitive data can leak through the AI supply chain, reinforcing the need to audit prompts and connected services.

top.title: Foundry Managed Compute is GA for serving open models on dedicated GPUs
top.summary: Foundry Managed Compute is generally available for running open models on dedicated GPUs, with Global and US or EU Data Zone deployments.
top.why: Compare it with self-managed GPU hosting when choosing how to serve open models, especially if deployment location is part of your data-residency design.

top.title: Azure Functions OpenAI Extension support ends April 20, 2027
top.summary: Support for the Azure Functions OpenAI Extension ends on April 20, 2027; Microsoft directs users to migrate to the OpenAI, Foundry, or Azure AI Search SDKs as appropriate.
top.why: Inventory Functions apps using the extension and schedule migration before the deadline to avoid relying on an unsupported integration.

top.title: Foundry previews custom post-training loops for open-weight models
top.summary: Programmed Training is a public preview API for building custom post-training loops over open-weight models, with access available by request.
top.why: If your model work needs more control than managed training jobs provide, assess this preview before building a separate training orchestration stack.

top.title: Foundry previews evaluation of full multi-turn agent conversations
top.summary: Multi-turn evaluation lets you assess complete agent conversations against quality standards rather than scoring responses one at a time.
top.why: Use conversation-level tests to catch failures that only emerge across turns before deciding an agent is ready for production.

top.title: Azure Firewall for Containers enters public preview
top.summary: Azure Firewall for Containers extends Azure Firewall protection to containerized workloads and provides centralized network-traffic controls.
top.why: Evaluate it if you need a centralized firewall approach for container workloads, but treat it as a preview rather than a production-ready dependency.

also.title: Foundry adds governance policy guidance in Canvas and VS Code
also.summary: Foundry Canvas and its VS Code toolkit now surface relevant policies and warnings for agent types, models, toolboxes, and guardrails.

also.title: Hybrid Logic Apps can now use SQL as a storage provider
also.summary: SQL storage for workflow runtime state is generally available for Hybrid Logic Apps running on customer-managed infrastructure, but not for Azure-hosted Logic Apps Standard.

also.title: Hybrid Logic Apps can use cached Integration Account artifacts offline
also.summary: Hybrid Logic Apps can cache supported Integration Account artifacts in local SQL storage and continue using them during temporary loss of Azure connectivity.

top.title: Two million AI supply-chain canaries expose sensitive-data leaks
top.summary: A test using two million prompts containing unique, trackable secrets found that sensitive data does not reliably stay private as it passes through the AI supply chain.
top.why: Review what prompt data is sent to models and third-party services, and test whether logs, integrations, or downstream tools expose information your users expect to remain private.

top.title: METR update finds AI task horizons still favor coding over judgment
top.summary: A new report from evaluation nonprofit METR updates its time-horizon analysis: some AI capabilities continue to improve exponentially, but models perform less well on tasks requiring judgment than on coding.
top.why: Avoid using coding progress alone to justify broader agent autonomy; evaluate the judgment-heavy tasks in your own workload separately.

also.title: Trump proposes a tax on US companies building data centers abroad
also.summary: Trump said he plans to impose a “tremendous tax” on US companies that build data centers outside the country, but the report provides no policy details.

also.title: Meta is reconsidering its 2030 net-zero goal as AI data-center emissions rise
also.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 sustainability goals amid record emissions associated with its AI data centers.

top.title: Meta introduces Triton extensions for lower-level GPU hardware control
top.summary: Meta developed Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX) to give GPU programmers lower-level execution control and access to advanced hardware capabilities than high-level GPU abstractions provide; the report does not establish its adoption or maturity.
top.why: If you build or tune custom GPU kernels, track whether TLX becomes a practical way to reach hardware features that standard Triton abstractions do not expose.

also.title: OpenSearch warns that agent failures can look successful in telemetry
also.summary: An agent can call the wrong API and still receive a valid response, so ordinary success-status monitoring may miss the failure.
